1 وَدَجَ , (S, K,) aor.
وَدِجَ , (S,) inf. n. وَدْجٌ (L, K) and وِدَاجٌ; (L;) and ↓ ودّج , inf. n. تَوْدِيجٌ; (K;) but the latter has an intensive signification; (Msb;) He cut the vein called الوَدَج: (K:) he bled a beast by cutting the vein so called; ودج with reference to a beast, as the object of the act, being the same as فَصَدَ with reference to a man. (S.) ―
-b2- وَدَجَ, inf. n. وَدْجٌ (tropical:) He put to rights; put into a right or proper state; adjusted. (S, K.) وَدَجَ المَالَ He put the property into a right or proper state. (Msb.) وَدَجَ بَيْنَ القَوْمِ He adjusted differences between the people, (S, Msb,) and put an end to evil. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
